title: Durable daemon session authority
description: Objective: land a production SqliteEventStore-backed principal/session/credential/capability authority, concrete proof-of-possession verifier, and durable replay guard for non-command transports. Depends on task-b4f12e63baca4ecc9f2c159ed3c3ad78. Before planning, obtain an explicit product decision for proof algorithm, canonical signed challenge bytes, key encoding, clock skew/TTL, renewal/rotation, and replay-key semantics; the pinned design leaves these open, so do not guess. NOT in scope: recipient/effect registries, coordination mailbox operations, MCP/HTTP listeners, or lifecycle command dispatch. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authority-contracts.ts, session-authority-contracts.js, session-authority.ts, session-authority.js, session-authority.test.ts. Production consumers: the coordination-recipient registry prerequisite and task-4afcb06422ed4adb89430b7ea9758d7f. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The approved versioned proof protocol freezes algorithm, canonical challenge bytes, key encoding, TTL/skew, renewal, rotation, and replay-key semantics; unsupported, malformed, missing, or unverifiable protocol facts refuse with exact stable core code and layer.

Production create/open/renew/rotate/close operations commit and read exact principal, session, credential generation/client key, transport scope/capability, and replay facts through SqliteEventStore with idempotent receipt/digest preservation across store recreation.

Authentication calls the reusable core session seam with the concrete verifier and durable replay evidence; callers cannot inject positive verifier, replay, session, or capability answers, and private keys, plaintext credentials, and presented proofs are never persisted or logged.

Focused real-file tests create authority only through production writers and prove valid recreation plus forged, expired, replayed, rotated, revoked, unknown-session, and missing-capability refusals with exact code and layer, zero authority, unchanged durable state where required, and nonzero generated-case counts.

The exact verification command exits 0, every production file remains below 400 lines, and a frozen read/auth surface supplies authenticated active-session facts to the two named consumers without command, recipient, effect, or mailbox authority.
taskRails: Planning is blocked until the proof protocol choices are explicitly confirmed; do not invent cryptographic or clock semantics.
Persist durable evidence and public-key material only; never persist plaintext credentials, private keys, or presented proofs.
Coordination capabilities remain explicit transport scopes; never synthesize RuntimeCommandKinds or colon-containing core capability IDs.

implementationPlan.description: Implement protocol v1 and concrete proof verification — create session-authority-protocol.ts plus its exact LF bridge. Snapshot exact own data properties once; build the domain plus eleven u32be-length-framed canonical scalar byte sequences in the approved order; expose the canonical challenge/request digest functions so production and tests share one surface. Validate safe integer/time bounds, lowercase hex lengths, canonical Ed25519 DER SPKI by createPublicKey/asymmetricKeyType/export round-trip, SHA-256 clientKeyId, and exact 64-byte signature before `node:crypto.verify(null,...)`; contain all crypto/parser throws as false. Surface: canonicalSessionProofBytes (domain `moe.session-proof.v1` + eleven u32be-length-framed scalars in the approved order principalId, projectId, sessionId, credentialId, generation, clientKeyId, transportId, requestId, requestDigest, issuedAt, nonce; strings UTF-8, safe integers unsigned decimal ASCII, hex fields as their lowercase-hex ASCII), sessionAuthorityRequestDigest (sorted-key canonical JSON, depth-bounded, safe-integer only), sessionReplayDigest (SHA-256 over the framed sessionId/generation/clientKeyId/nonce tuple under a `/replay` domain, so no raw nonce can be returned or persisted), sessionClientKeyId / isCanonicalSessionPublicKey (lowercase-hex 44-byte DER SPKI, createPublicKey + asymmetricKeyType==="ed25519" + export round-trip equality, then SHA-256 of the SPKI bytes), readSessionProof (exact 5-key snapshot, protocolVersion 1, algorithm Ed25519, 16-byte lowercase-hex nonce, 64-byte lowercase-hex signature, inclusive 60s age / 30s future skew), verifySessionProofSignature and verifySessionProofOverChallenge (node:crypto.verify(null,...) with every crypto/parser throw contained as false). implementationPlan.description: Implement durable folding and the authority service — create session-authority-store.ts/.js and session-authority.ts/.js. In the store leaf, namespace deterministic principal/session/replay aggregates, page all aggregate events, strictly decode exact schema/event payloads, return UNKNOWN on any gap/unknown/malformed bytes, and use only public SqliteEventStore commitExpectedVersionDecision/read APIs. Store fixed-order redacted request/result bytes and public facts/digests; return the original persisted mutation result/receipt on replay and delegate version/store failures with their exact code under DURABLE_STORE. In the service factory, expose frozen createPrincipal/openSession/renewSession/rotateCredential/closeSession/authenticate/readSessionAuthority/readActiveSession methods. Build all core records through createPrincipal/createSession/createCredential/rotateCredential; open requires the durable principal and a fresh self-proof; renew/rotate/close require current core authentication. `authenticate` owns concrete verifyProof/checkReplay closures, commits the hashed replay marker at expected version 0, passes only durable records into authenticateSession, and returns a module-private nominally branded frozen success with sessionVersion/authorityDigest/replayDigest. Re-read current state for readActiveSession; CLOSED/expired/generation/key/profile/project mismatches never become active. Keep each production .ts <=250 where practical and strictly below 400.
implementationPlan.note:
Durable fold and authority service landed; the focused suite is GREEN at 16/16 and the whole daemon suite is 41 files / 767 tests passing.

STORE LEAF (session-authority-store.ts, 387 lines + exact LF bridge): namespaced `moe.session-authority.v1/{principal,session,replay}/<id>` aggregates; `readAllEvents` pages every aggregate page and refuses any aggregateSequence gap; `decodePayload` requires the exact domainSchemaVersion and a fatal-UTF-8 JSON object; the fold requires SessionAuthorityOpened first, refuses any event after CLOSED, and every record is minted by the core factories createPrincipal/createSession/createCredential so the fold cannot invent its own shapes. Any gap, unknown type, foreign schema, or malformed payload returns UNKNOWN, never a partial positive. `commitAuthorityDecision` is the single mutation seam: it pre-checks the decision for a foreign commandKind under the kind-less decision key, commits canonical fixed-key-order request/result bytes through commitExpectedVersionDecision, surfaces a NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT expected-version conflict under its own code, and maps IDEMPOTENCY/COMMAND_ID/DURABLE_ID conflicts to SESSION_AUTHORITY_COMMAND_CONFLICT and everything else to its exact DurableStoreErrorCode, all under DURABLE_STORE. `observeReplayMarker` burns only the hashed identity at expected version 0.

SERVICE (session-authority.ts, 392 lines + exact LF bridge): frozen createPrincipal/openSession/renewSession/rotateCredential/closeSession/authenticate/readSessionAuthority/readActiveSession. Open requires the durable principal plus a fresh self-proof whose requestDigest binds the profile revision, key, scopes, and generation 1. Authenticate owns concrete verifyProof/checkReplay closures over durable material only and passes durable records into core authenticateSession; the presented input carries no verdict callbacks. Renew/rotate/close each require a fresh current-generation authentication, and each commit answers from a re-read fold rather than from what the module intended to write.

DESIGN NOTE worth QA's attention: authenticate binds core's session record to the clientKeyId of the PRESENTED credential's own durable record, not to the current one. Without that, a superseded generation is rejected at core BINDING as an unbound key and can never reach the GENERATION layer the DoD requires. The key is durable material either way, and on the success path the presented credential is the current one, so the returned facts stay truthful.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review and five mutation drills done. Every drill was applied to PRODUCTION, run, and reverted; `sha256sum -c` over all nine owned paths reports OK for all nine afterwards, and the focused suite is green again at 16/16.

DRILL 1 - bypass real Ed25519 verification (verifyProof closure returns true): RED in 2 tests. The forged `signatureHex: "00".repeat(64)` case returned ok:true with facts and a burned replay receipt instead of AUTHENTICATION_FAILED/PROOF.
DRILL 2 - bypass durable replay refusal (always answer FRESH): RED in 3 tests, and this is the strongest evidence for epic rail 6. The outcome stayed `ok:false` at the SAME layer REPLAY while only the code moved SESSION_REPLAYED -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, and the tests still went red. An "asserted only that it refused" suite would have stayed green.
DRILL 3 - bypass generation revocation (rebuild the core credential at the current generation, revoked:false): RED in 2 tests; the superseded-generation request authenticated instead of SESSION_REPLAYED/GENERATION.
DRILL 4 - bypass transport matching (append the presented transportId to the session scopes): RED in 1 test; the unlisted transport authenticated instead of CAPABILITY_DENIED/TRANSPORT.
DRILL 5 - swap the first two entries of the production CHALLENGE_ORDER: RED in the byte-exact framing pin.

HONEST LIMIT ON DRILL 5, disclosed rather than glossed: only the pinned-bytes test caught it, not the real-signature tests. That is structural, not a gap in coverage - epic rail 6 requires tests to sign through the PRODUCTION encoder, so signer and verifier reorder together and stay self-consistent. The byte-exact literal is therefore the only defence against frame-order drift, which is exactly why the mis-transcribed literal I found and corrected at step 5 mattered.

planningNotes.risks: Canonical signed bytes must not drift: protocol v1 is ASCII domain `moe.session-proof.v1` followed by fixed-order u32be-length-prefixed frames for principalId, projectId, sessionId, credentialId, generation, clientKeyId, transportId, requestId, requestDigest, issuedAt, and nonce. Encode strings as UTF-8, safe integers as unsigned decimal ASCII without leading zeros, and digest/key/nonce fields as their required lowercase-hex ASCII spelling before framing; tests pin exact bytes, not a duplicate encoder. Require canonical Ed25519 DER SPKI round-trip, SHA-256(SPKI) clientKeyId, exactly 64-byte lowercase-hex signatures, 128-bit lowercase-hex nonce, <=60s proof age and <=30s future skew. Accept proof at the inclusive TTL/skew boundaries and refuse one millisecond beyond. Session expiry is exclusive, initial/renewal TTL is 15 minutes, and absolute lifetime is 8 hours from open; renewal changes only expiry. Rotation keeps session/principal/scopes/expiry, increments generation exactly once, revokes the old credential, installs the new public key/credential, and verifies both old and new signatures over the same challenge bytes whose requestDigest binds the proposed new material. Store only public key/material and digests: never raw signature, nonce, challenge, proof object, plaintext credential, or private key. An unreadable/unknown event fold is UNKNOWN/BINDING and never a partial positive record. A valid proof may burn its replay digest before a later core generation/state/expiry/transport refusal, matching core's fixed precedence; tests distinguish authority state (unchanged) from the append-only replay fact. Idempotent mutation replay still authenticates where a current session is required and returns the original stored receipt/result bytes.
